subject: rmr2 with gzip and bzip2 input data

messages.author: 6a098c82358311ab
messages.subject: rmr2 with gzip and bzip2 input data
parts: I know hadoop can work with gzip and bzip2 compressed data. Are there any issues using rmr2 with either of these formats? I did a quick test about a week ago and it seemed like it failed to read the data. The files are DEL delimited text files that have been compressed due to their size. I am aware of hadoops regular issues with gzip files and splitting them but that's not currently a concern.

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#485] rmr2 with gzip and bzip2 input data
parts:
This is the first report I hear but I've never tested it explicitly. I've worked successfully with lzo compressed data in the past. rmr relies on hadoop for compression and decompression and user code doesn't need any changes. If you could provide a more complete bug report I'd be happy to look into it. Also it would be interesting to know if hadoop can read the data, no rmr involved, like hadoop fs -get filename (a small one or you may run into trouble)  and then inspect the data to see if it's been decompressed. Thanks


Antonio

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#485] rmr2 with gzip and bzip2 input data
parts:
I've finally managed to get back to this and have confirmed that rHadoop can work with gzip and bzip2 archives, but I have had some weird behaviour.

My normal DEL delimited data was not returning anything, so I decided to simply and tested with this data set:

apples,1
orange,2
grapes,3
apple,2
apple,1
orange,1

using the fruit names as keys and summing the numbers. A python test gives me my expected result:

apples 4
grapes 3
orange 3

When I run it through rhadoop on non-archived data I do not get the fruit names. Instead I get:

1 4
2 4
3 2

When I run it on either bzip2 or gzip archves the counts are right but I still have issues with the key names:

1 4
2 3
3 3

I've been beating my head against a wall trying to figure out what's causing these issues and any help would be very appreciated!

This is my script:

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript

require('rmr2');
require('rhdfs');

categoryCount = function (input, output) {

  mapreduce(
    input = input,
    output = output,
    input.format = make.input.format("csv", sep = ","),
    output.format = 'text',
    map = function(k, fields) {
      keyval(fields[[1]], fields[[2]])
    },
    reduce = function(key, vv) {
      keyval(key, sum(vv))
    }
  )
}

hdfs.init()

if ( hdfs.exists("/user/michael/ccCount") ) {

  hdfs.rmr("/user/michael/ccCount")
  print("Removed directory from previous run.")
}

categoryCount("/user/michael/fruit.csv", "/user/michael/ccCount/")
#categoryCount("/user/michael/fruit.csv.gz", "/user/michael/ccCount/")
#categoryCount("/user/michael/fruit.csv.bz2", "/user/michael/ccCount/")

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#488] rmr2 with gzip and bzip2 input data
parts:
I guess your strings are being converted to factors. Try the additional argument stringAsFactors = FALSE to make.input.format.


Antonio
